newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says 31 firms qualify for debut warrants.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says 31 firms qualify for debut warrants.

text.p: The Taiwan Stock Exchange said on Monday 31 listed firms qualified for warrant issues, the latest instrument to be pioneered in Taiwan's liberalising financial system.

In a long-expected decree effective from Sunday, June 1, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said local and foreign banks or securities brokerages with T$3 billion or more in registered capital could issue warrants on qualified shares.

As of late Monday, the stock exchange said no institution had yet applied to be among the first to list warrants, which have never been allowed in Taiwan despite the market's relative maturity and massive turnover.
The stock exchange, which is managing warrant issuance under the SEC's guidance and will list the instruments, initially said 24 listed firms had met the miminum criteria for inclusion in warrants.
A further seven were added on Monday, exchange officials told Reuters.

To qualify, a listed firm's Taiwan shares must have a total market value, based on May 31 closing prices, of more than T$25 billion, with at least 20 percent their shares circulating in the market between January 31 and April 30, officials said.
Listed firms also must have more than 15,000 shareholders -- at least 7,000 of whom hold 1,000 to 50,000 shares.

The seven newly qualified firms are: Compal Electronics, Yageo Corp, Acer Peripherals Corp, Pacific Construction, Med Bank Hsin Chu, Fubon Insurance and Fuh-Hwa Securities, the exchange said in a statement.

The initial 24 are: Taiwan Cement, Taiwan Tea, President Enterprise, Nan Ya Plastics, Formosa Plastics, China Petrochemical, Hualon, Shinkong Synthetic Fiber, Tatung, Teco Electric & Machinery Co Ltd, Pacific Electric Wire, Walsin Lihwa, China Steel, United Microelectro nics, Acer, First International Computer, Winbond, Cathay Construction, China Development, Taipei Business Bank, Medium Business Bank of Tainan, Taichung Business Bank, Chinatrust Commercial Bank and Farmers Bank of China. (US$1 = T$27.8)
